question.problem:
A function $g(x)$ has values according to the table below:

| **$x$** | $0.6$ | $0.8$ | $1$ | $1.2$ | $1.4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $g(x)$ | $2.6$ | $1.9$ | $1.5$ | $2.3$ | $5.9$ |

$$

$$

Approximate ${g}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=0.8$ using a central difference approximation.

${g}^{′}(0.8)≈$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{g}^{′}(x)≈\frac{g(x+h)-g(x-h)}{2h}
$$

 
at the point $x=0.8.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=0.2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(0.8) & ≈\frac{g(0.8+0.2)-g(0.8-0.2)}{2(0.2)} \\  & =\frac{g(1)-g(0.6)}{2(0.2)} \\  & =\frac{1.5-2.6}{0.4} \\  & =\frac{-1.1}{0.4} \\  & =\frac{-11}{4} \\  & =-2.75.\end{aligned}
$$
